fix.shows: Part III Action Research & Resource Centre, a legal aid group with offices in New Delhi and Patna, wrote this guide for Delhi's electors and says it grew out of helping survivors of domestic violence apply in the revision. It covers who is eligible, the enumeration form on paper or online, finding a name in the draft roll and in Delhi's list of notices, Forms 6, 7 and 8, the documents to keep ready, hearings and the two appeals. It gives the 1950 helpline, the Commission's complaint routes and where to go for help without the internet. Its dates for Delhi are the ones the Commission set on 29 October, with claims and objections until 25 November, notices decided by 15 December and the final roll on 22 December. Its table of forms gives Form 7 for an elector whose own name was wrongly deleted. Form 7 is the form for objecting to a name on the roll, and the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls of 2023 says a person no longer on the roll applies again on Form 6. The guide is in English and Hindi.
fix.note: Shared by the owner as https://share.google/fNIKY7QGWAQOUIFZT, which redirects through https://www.google.com/share.google?q=fNIKY7QGWAQOUIFZT to the post on part-three.org, dated 26 October 2026 (article:published_time 2026-10-26T10:03:29Z, modified 2026-10-30T10:44:48Z), byline 'Part III Team'. The post links the English PDF, https://part-three.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/sir-eng-1.pdf (32 pages, Canva, created 30 October 2026, sha256 3ea72362dd839293b5ba13d5b1e8c3e369d29d51860f6db59e9889820287f00a), read in full with pdftotext on 31 October 2026. A Hindi post and PDF (sir-hindi-1.pdf, 32 pages, created 30 October 2026) carry the same dates. The quote is the opening of the credits page. Delhi's dates in the guide (start 30 June 2026, draft 31 August, claims and objections to 25 November, notice, hearing and disposal to 15 December, final roll 22 December) match the Delhi schedule in data/india/process.json. Its figures of over 97 lakh in the draft and 33.13 lakh notices match the Delhi summary (97,53,577 and 33,12,919). One point disagrees with the sources the site uses, and the summary states it once. The table on printed page 16 gives Form 7 where 'your name was wrongfully deleted', and page 18 counts the same case as an objection. The site's help page has Form 7 as the objection to a name (remedies.json form7, from the form's own title, 'Objection for Proposed Inclusion/ Deletion of Name in Existing Electoral Roll') and Form 6 for a person no longer on the roll (remedies.json form6, from the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls, Document 10, Edition 2, March 2023, para 14.7.4.1, page 127: 'he/she need to apply for addition of the name again through Form-6 (as a new elector)'). Page 17 says an elector whose enumeration form was not handed in can apply only on Form 6 during claims and objections, which is the Commission's instruction (process.json forms, order of 24 June 2025). At the Supreme Court hearing of 28 October (court-54) the bench said electors on the 2026 roll left off the draft should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8, but no order was reported, so the guide is not faulted for following the instruction and the point is left out of the summary. The guide's account of the online and offline appeal (page 21 to 23: an 'Appeal Against Order' dashboard, a 2 MB file limit, an automated SMS) and its statement that ECI guidelines prohibit demanding notarised copies were not found in any source the site holds and are not carried. The credits name the researchers and designer; they are not carried, and the byline on the post is used.

The quote is the credits page (PDF page 2, unnumbered), verbatim. Every point of coverage is in the guide: eligibility (p. 6), the enumeration form with the BLO (pp. 7 to 11) and online (p. 12), the draft list and Delhi's notice list (pp. 13 to 15), the table of Forms 6, 7 and 8 (p. 16), Form 6 documents (p. 17), claims, objections, notices, hearing documents and the appeal under section 24 to the DM within 15 days and the CEO within 30 (pp. 18 to 20), online and offline appeals (pp. 21 to 23), the 1950 helpline, complaints@eci.gov.in, NGSP, Book-a-Call and the Voter Helpline App, and help without digital access (p. 24). Delhi's dates (p. 5: claims and objections to 25 November, notice, hearing and disposal up to 15 December, final roll 22 December 2026) match the Delhi entry of 29 October in data/india/process.json. 'A legal aid group with offices in New Delhi and Patna' rests on the back cover ('Part III has offices in New Delhi and Patna') and part-three.org/our-work-2-2/ ('We provide legal aid to survivors of identity- and gender-based violence'). (1) The Form 7 point is kept: printed page 16 lists Form 7 for 'your name was wrongfully deleted' and page 18 calls that an objection, and the site holds a sourced statement of the manual's rule in remedies.json form6 (Manual on Electoral Rolls, March 2023, para 14.7.4.1, page 127), so the clause stands with the manual named. Page 17 follows the Commission's instruction, and court-54 records only what the bench said, with no order reported. Setting a guide against remarks that carry no order is a criticism the guide does not earn, and it put a second disagreement in a summary that should state one.
